questions.question: Q1. What does the Pulse Transfer Function relate in discrete systems?

answers.a: It relates the output to the input in the continuous-time domain.
answers.b: It relates the output to the input in the discrete-time domain.
answers.c: It defines the relationship between input and output in the frequency domain.
answers.d: It is only used in continuous systems.

questions.question: Q2. Which of the following is the primary purpose of the Pulse Transfer Function?

answers.a: To describe the system behaviour in the time domain.
answers.b: To determine the system's stability in the continuous-time domain.
answers.c: To model the dynamics of a discrete-time system.
answers.d: To convert continuous systems to discrete systems.

questions.question: Q3. The region of convergence (ROC) of a discrete-time system’s Pulse Transfer Function determines:

answers.a: The frequency response of the system.
answers.b: The input-output relationship of the system.
answers.c: The impulse response of the system.

questions.question: Q4. What is the primary advantage of representing a discrete-time system in state-space form?

answers.a: It is easier to compute the system’s transfer function.
answers.b: It allows for easy representation of multi-input, multi-output (MIMO) systems.
answers.d: It is simpler than transfer function modelling.

questions.question: Q5. In the z-domain, the poles of the Pulse Transfer Function are important for:

answers.a: Defining the system's stability and behaviour.
answers.d: Designing the input signal for the system.
